title: Hebrews: hold on to Jesus
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Hebrews begins like a sermon and ends like a letter, and no one knows who wrote it.
It was written to believers who had once suffered bravely, and were now tired, drifting, and tempted to give up on Christ.

scripture.text: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son

lines: Teaching and urging take turns. Jesus is greater than the angels and Moses. He is a high priest like Melchizedek, and the one offering the tabernacle pointed toward.
From chapter ten, the call is to draw near and endure.

scripture.text: the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.

lines: God, who spoke through the prophets, has spoken last and best in his Son.
The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature.
The Son is also fully human: made like his brothers, tempted, crying out with tears.

scripture.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature

lines: The word better runs through the book. The old covenant is a shadow, not because it was false, but because it pointed ahead. The writer honors it as God's gift.
This book was misused to teach contempt for the Jewish people. That misuse was wrong.

scripture.text: For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come

lines: Hebrews alone calls Jesus a priest at length. He offered not animals but himself, once for all, and sat down because the work was finished.
He was tempted in every way, yet without sin, so he can sympathize.
He always lives to intercede for them.

scripture.text: He always lives to intercede for them.

lines: Five solemn warnings not to drift or turn away run beside as many words of hope. They're addressed to people the writer believes will persevere. How they relate to assurance is much debated, and this film takes no side.
Then come the roll call of faith, and the race.
Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith.

scripture.text: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith

lines: Start with chapter one, then eleven and twelve. The key chapters are one, two, four, six, seven, nine, eleven, and twelve.
Read with the Old Testament texts it builds on open beside it, and watch for the word better.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

scripture.text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
